newsitem.title: CANADA: Amoco Canada picks Sedco as offshore driller.
newsitem.headline: Amoco Canada picks Sedco as offshore driller.

text.p: Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd said on Tuesday it selected Sedco Forex, a division of Schlumberger Ltd, as drilling contractor for its 1997 drilling program off the east coast of Canada.
Amoco said the rig being contracted for the program, on Newfoundland's Grand Banks, was the semi-submersible mobile unit known as the "Bill Shoemaker."

The project is part of a recent wave of oil exploration interest off Canada's east coast and follows the Hibernia development, set for startup up next year, and Terra Nova, which still requires final project approval.

"The East Coast's ongoing infrastructure activity, complemented by Newfoundland's royalty announcement last June, provides better certainty for these types of exploration ventures," Bob Erickson, Amoco Canada's new chairman and president, said in a statement.

The company said its drilling program, in the Grand Banks' Jeanne d'Arc Basin, was slated to start in May 1997 and would include at least one well on the West Bonne Bay prospect, located 15 km northeast of Terra Nova and 40 km southeast of Hibernia.
Amoco acquired the acreage in late 1995. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
